takeaway: Posterior cruciate ligament: lateral surface of medial femoral condyle to the posterior tibia; two bundles; intracapsular but extrasynovial; main role is to prevent posterior displacement of the tibia.

question.text: Which of the following statements regarding the posterior cruciate ligament is correct?

answer.text: It prevents posterior dislocation of the tibia.

lines.text: The posterior cruciate ligament sits in the middle of the knee, between the femur and the tibia.
It attaches to the lateral surface of the medial femoral condyle, not the lateral condyle.
It is made of two bundles, not three.
And it is intracapsular but extrasynovial, so it is not intrasynovial.
Its main job is to stop the tibia from sliding backwards on the femur.
So the correct statement is that it prevents posterior displacement of the tibia.
